Optional: exact HTF anchor by scanning chart bars inside the HTF pivot bar for high==px (bounded by f_tfRatio and anchorMax).
proposals.risk: Touches all drawing code, so there is regression risk (alignment of label and tether). Holiday schedule changes within the next N bars can shift the right edge by a bar (cosmetic).

proposals.title: Slow-ATR pool geometry and an order-block volatility filter
proposals.rationale: Open-source SMC uses ATR(200) or a cumulative mean range for EQH tolerance, OB filtering and IFVG width. The engine uses ATR(14) for eqPx (1522), wPx (1520), the test band (654) and the stack window (1926), which shrink 2-3x in quiet sessions, so Asia equal lows stop merging. LuxAlgo also excludes candles with range >= 2*ATR(200) from becoming OBs; the engine can pick a capitulation candle (1677-1680, 1720-1723), making a multi-ATR zone whose near edge sits almost at price.
proposals.spec: Input geomIn ['Fast (14)', 'Max (14/200)'] in G_LIQ; atrG = geomIn=='Fast (14)' ? atr : atrE (after 878). Use atrG at 1520, 1522 and 1926-1927 and in the test band (pass separately to track so maxAway stays on atr). OB candidate loops 1677/1720: also require (high[k]-low[k]) < 2*nz(atrSlow[k], atr), falling back to the current rule if none qualifies. Input obMaxH 1.5: if obT-obB > obMaxH*atr, use the candle body (the body option of open-source OB and breaker scripts). Measure OB/BRK and CHART LIQ family EDGE by toggling.
proposals.risk: Under 'Max', quiet-session tolerances are wider than today, so slightly more EQ merges and stack memberships; measurable via the toggle.

proposals.title: iFVG significance filter and show-last-N per side (Clean clutter control)
proposals.rationale: Every FVG >= 0.15*ATR(14) is tracked (1877, 1887) and each inversion draws a box (up to 8, 198/1620), which clutters the Clean view on 1-3 minute charts. LuxAlgo IFVG filters by width with an ATR multiplier and shows only the last N per side. Evidence shows iFVG retests carry no edge (38% vs 38%), so this is purely visual.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_IFVG): ifvgMinW 0.25 (x atrE), ifvgShow 2 per side. At inversion (1603) also require (z.top - z.bottom) >= ifvgMinW*atrE; otherwise drop it from fvgTrk without creating an iFVG or alert. In rendering (2145-2149), walk ifvgs newest-first, keep the first ifvgShow per dir visible and set the others' bgcolor and border to transparency 100; they stay tracked and cleaned normally.
proposals.risk: Some users want every inversion shown; the input allows up to 10.

proposals.title: LVNs as profile troughs (local minima against neighbouring rows) instead of an absolute 30%-of-peak cut
proposals.rationale: The engine marks any contiguous run below 0.30*peak as an LVN (2260-2269), which in skewed profiles is a broad shoulder, not the thin node between two acceptance areas. Open-source node detection (LuxAlgo) defines a trough as a row lower than N neighbouring rows on each side; practitioners place LVNs between two HVNs.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_LVN): lvnNbr 8 (% of rows), lvnProm 0.15 (x peak). N = max(1, round(rows*lvnNbr/100)). For r in [N, rows-1-N]: let v = vpSm[r], lMax/rMax = max of the N rows on each side. A trough requires v strictly below every row in both neighbourhoods (strict local minimum) and min(lMax, rMax) - v >= lvnProm*peak. Grow the zone while neighbouring rows are <= v + 0.35*(min(lMax, rMax) - v). Keep tail exclusion and lvnN per side. The path-cost multiplier is unchanged; a trough/peak-aware path cost belongs to ICT-5 and can be A/B'd via the usePathVP toggle.
proposals.risk: None to selection; display only.

result.summary: The engine is already ahead of nearly every surveyed competitor on substance. No other tool combines multi-source pools, PD arrays, a multi-pillar score, an empirical PoT and a ledger that grades itself against a distance-matched random-level baseline. Most commercial and free DOL tools pick the target with a one-line rule: nearest opposing pool (ICT Order Block Pro, ICT doctrine), tier weight divided by ATR distance (LuxAlgo DOL: W 4, D 3, session/EQ 2, gaps 1.5, swings 1), or a volume-weighted side share of at least 55% (HS_16). None of them publishes accuracy. The only "keeps score" competitors (ForexCracked, 2,239 boosts; Flux sweep profiler) measure per-category reach or edge and print n next to every figure, but neither tests against a null nor commits to one target. Where the engine loses is UX hygiene. The legend prints 75 input values, because no input sets display (the reference screenshot shows only the name). The Clean label shows PoT to one decimal with no horizon or sample size, and shows "PoT: 95.0%" for a target already reached (line 2067). Alerts are static text with no approach, abandoned or JSON events. On a white chart the Classic neon palette is illegible (#39FF14 is 1.36:1 against WCAG's 3:1 for graphics and 4.5:1 for text). The best tools converge on six conventions: one target confirmed at bar close; an explicit balanced/no-draw state instead of a forced pick; a probability shown with its horizon and n; rest/swept/broken lifecycle with ghosts; distance filtering so far levels neither clutter nor compress the chart; and few, filterable, JSON-capable alerts. No competitor benchmarks itself against the simple rules others ship. In M4, only 17 of 50 methods beat a simple combination benchmark, so running nearest-pool and tier/distance "shadow selectors" in the ledger is the most valuable novel addition: it proves or disproves the value of the multi-pillar score and gives an A/B harness for every later change. Traders on Reddit ask which DOL is active, when it will hit, on what timeframe, and where to take profit. They complain about inconsistency, clutter and squashed charts. The reference product's 259 comments are almost all trial requests. Evidence for UX features is weak for forecasting value. The strong evidence is on communication: natural frequencies raised correct Bayesian answers from 7% to 45%, precise numbers read as confidence, and alert fatigue produces about 90% override rates. Proposals avoid overlap with the other reports (calibrated PoT, target lock, clock horizon, sweep-outcome logic, path resistance) and provide the display and alert layers for them.

concepts.name: Nearest-opposing-pool selection
concepts.definition: Target = argmin distance over untapped liquidity pools on the bias side (or opposite a validated setup). ICT doctrine: 'the NEAREST significant pool in the direction of the bias', matched to trade duration. ICT Order Block Pro projects a dashed DOL line from a validated OB to the closest opposing BSL/SSL.
concepts.dolRole: Simplest 'where next' rule. Maximises raw hit rate because targets are close, so it is the natural benchmark for any scorer.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published accuracy. Doctrine and vendor descriptions only (theinnercircletraders.com; tradingview.com/script/oObsuObl).
concepts.engineNotes: Not used as a rule or as a benchmark. Proximity is only one pillar (evaluate, lines 661-706). COMP-3 adds it as a shadow selector.

concepts.name: Tier-over-distance selection
concepts.definition: score = tierWeight / distATR, with tiers weekly 4, daily 3, session and equal extremes 2, gaps 1.5, swings 1. The best score on the structure-bias side (structure length 50) is the working draw, with fallback to the other side. Swing length 10, EQ tolerance 0.1 ATR, minimum gap 0.5 ATR, maximum pool age 500 bars. Re-anchors to the next objective on a sweep.
concepts.dolRole: Ranks pools by significance per unit of distance. The free alternative users will compare us against.
concepts.evidenceNotes: LuxAlgo DOL page gives the formula but no accuracy figures.
concepts.engineNotes: Tier enters density (f_tierW line 506, used at 682) but the rule is never benchmarked. COMP-3 adds it as shadow selector S2.

concepts.name: Per-side draw states incl. Two-Sided / No Draw
concepts.definition: Each side gets a 0-100 score (pool quality, ATR proximity, trend backbone, freshness). States: Buy-Side Draw, Sell-Side Draw, Two-Sided (score gap below the balance-gap input), No Draw (no qualifying untapped pool in range). AGPro v1.2 suppresses runway, target and invalidation for balanced or low-score states.
concepts.dolRole: Abstains when neither side dominates, so precision improves where the tool does commit.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Selective classification (Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017, arXiv:1705.08500) supports abstention plus coverage reporting. The AGPro convention itself is weak evidence.
concepts.engineNotes: dirSide 0 internally (line 1895). Terminal shows BALANCED (2342) and 'scanning…' (2367). Clean shows nothing. Counter-draw fallback always forces a target. No coverage metric. COMP-6 adds the state.

concepts.name: Target commitment (confirm at close / lock / hysteresis)
concepts.definition: Target changes only on confirmed bars (ASXLT: 'confirmed at candle close to reduce unnecessary intrabar switching'). HS_16 locks the target until it is hit, stopped, or N bars pass. The engine requires a challenger to lead by hyst (twice that across sides) for 2 consecutive bars.
concepts.dolRole: Stability. Jumping targets are the main trust killer and inflate false switches.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Convention across vendors. No measured benefit published.
concepts.engineNotes: Lines 2011-2020 plus off-killzone multiplier at 976. Hard lock mode belongs to SMC-2 (smc_impl.md).

concepts.name: Theoretical first-passage PoT with explicit horizon
concepts.definition: P(max over horizon T >= level) for a random walk from log-return volatility. Without drift the reflection principle gives P(touch) = 2 P(end beyond) (options rule PoT ~ 2 x P(ITM)). ASXLT horizons: 24 chart candles, 24 minutes, 1 h, 4 h, custom. Options always state expiry.
concepts.dolRole: Probability of reaching the target within a stated time. The horizon is part of the forecast.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Exact under the model; real prices deviate. Schwab, Option Alpha and tastytrade conventions.
concepts.engineNotes: f_pot / f_potModel (434, 1303) capped at 0.95. Horizon H = 30 bars is never displayed in Clean (2225) or the tooltip (2206). Clock horizon belongs to TIME-4. COMP-4 adds horizon display.

concepts.name: Measured reach frequency per category with sample size
concepts.definition: Per pool category x birth distance: reached within 50 bars (capped at 60). Touches split into rejected (close >= 1 ATR back inside within 20 bars), cut (close >= 0.5 ATR beyond) and stall. Printed only when n >= 20, else 'building'. Labels read 'reach X% of N'. Right-censoring fixed by counting only after the window elapses.
concepts.dolRole: Empirical base rates of which pool types actually get taken and how fast.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ForexCracked map (2,239 boosts) publishes the method, not validated results. The principle (empirical frequencies) is sound.
concepts.engineNotes: Empirical surface is by distance and HTF regime, not by category (f_empPoT 1284). Per-family hit rates appear in the Full view only. Category lift belongs to ICT-1.

concepts.name: Natural-frequency display (k of n next to %)
concepts.definition: Show counts beside probabilities (e.g. '41 of 63 reached'), with a minimum-sample gate before printing.
concepts.dolRole: Lets traders judge how much to trust a PoT value. Improves probabilistic reasoning.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Hoffrage et al. 2015 Front Psychol 6:1473: 7% vs 45% correct Bayesian inferences (Study 1, N = 64); replicated since Gigerenzer & Hoffrage 1995.
concepts.engineNotes: Clean label 2225 and tooltip 2206 show no n. n appears only in the Terminal accuracy header (2379). No PoT reliability buckets. COMP-4.

concepts.name: Probability display precision
concepts.definition: Number of digits and rounding steps used for displayed probabilities. Weather PoP is rounded to 10% (Canada) or 5% (UK Met Office); NWS wording bands: 20% slight chance, 30-50% chance, 60-70% likely.
concepts.dolRole: Over-precise displays signal more confidence than the model has.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Jerez-Fernandez, Angulo, Oppenheimer 2014 Psych Science 25(2):633-635: more digits are read as more confidence.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed '0.0' format at 2225 (it matches the reference look). No precision option. COMP-4 adds one, default unchanged.

concepts.name: Reached-target state display
concepts.definition: Once the target trades, the readout says it was reached instead of showing a probability.
concepts.dolRole: Avoids misreading a completed draw as a live forecast.
concepts.evidenceNotes: UX convention: Terminal already shows a SWEPT state; competitors mark hits.
concepts.engineNotes: Line 2067 sets activePoT := 0.95 on a live sweep, so the Clean label prints 'PoT: 95.0%' for a hit target. Terminal prints '✕ SWEPT ▸' (2237). COMP-4 fixes this.

concepts.name: Level lifecycle (rest / swept / broken) and ghosting
concepts.definition: Swept = wick through and close back on the original side within a confirmation window (Flux: 0 means same bar; ProEA: on the closed candle). Broken = close beyond, or the window expires; a swept level later closed beyond becomes broken. Ghost = kept at low opacity (ICT Order Block Pro: 25%; LuxAlgo 'Keep Swept Pools'). 'Past window' = faded once the reach window has passed.
concepts.dolRole: Swept-and-rejected pools imply reversal toward the opposite pool; broken pools imply continuation. This bears on the next draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ProEA code-read: none of the 15 most-boosted PDH/PDL scripts tells sweep from break. Outcome statistics belong to the ict_liq.md domain.
concepts.engineNotes: Strict trade-through removal (touched, 623). Raid hold/reject folded into D (1580-1582). Ghost labels '✕ SWEPT', '⊘ EJECTED' (1586) and '⊘ INVALIDATED' (2023), off by default. No swept-vs-broken display. Logic belongs to ICT-2; stamps in COMP-5.

concepts.name: Self-measurement ledger against a null
concepts.definition: Grade every asserted target over H bars against the base rate of a random level at the same distance. Wilson interval, cluster-robust z, verdict, bars-to-hit, MAE heat, first-touch race against invalidation.
concepts.dolRole: The only honest way to know whether the selected liquidity actually gets taken more often than chance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Standard forecast-evaluation methodology. No competitor does this (ForexCracked and Flux report raw rates or edge ratios without a null).
concepts.engineNotes: f_openTrial / f_step / f_book (1426-1500), f_potBase (1314), panel 2376-2430. Terminal only.

concepts.name: Benchmark against simple competitor rules (shadow selectors)
concepts.definition: Run the nearest-pool and tier/distance selectors in parallel on the same pool and bars, book their trials the same way, and compare edge over the distance-matched baseline (never raw hit rate).
concepts.dolRole: Shows whether the complex score predicts which liquidity is taken next better than the free rules do. Also an A/B harness for every change.
concepts.evidenceNotes: M4 (Makridakis et al. 2018 IJF 34(4):802-808): only 17 of 50 methods beat the Comb benchmark; ML methods ranked 23-57 of 60.
concepts.engineNotes: Not present. COMP-3.

concepts.name: Outcome stamps / result display
concepts.definition: On-chart markers of each target's fate: hit in N bars (optionally with PoT at assertion), abandoned with reason, expired. FIFO-capped. Examples: HS_16 'result display duration', Flux Active Sweep Tracker, ForexCracked purge circle, P2P Daily Streak.
concepts.dolRole: Makes timing (bars-to-hit) and hit rate visible per target. Supports replay testing and earned trust.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions only.
concepts.engineNotes: Trials hold bars, mae and status (375-396, 1434-1459), but nothing is drawn. COMP-5.

concepts.name: Approach alert
concepts.definition: Fires once per target when price comes within X of the target. ForexCracked: within 0.25 ATR of a category with reach >= 70% and meaningful n. ProEA: within 0.15 x daily ATR. edgeful: within 10 points.
concepts.dolRole: Timing: lets the trader prepare exits or entries as the draw completes. Approach-to-hit conversion is measurable.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions.
concepts.engineNotes: Not in the alert block (2077-2094). COMP-2.

concepts.name: Alert event coverage (abandoned / reached-at-close with result)
concepts.definition: Alerts when the committed target is replaced, ejected or invalidated, and a bar-close 'reached' event with bars-to-hit and MAE. HS_16 alerts on invalidation; LuxAlgo DOL alerts 'draw reached' and draw flips in both directions.
concepts.dolRole: Tells the trader the forecast changed or completed, and with what result.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions.
concepts.engineNotes: Events exist in code (ejection at 1584-1590, replacement and invalidation at 2021-2035) but raise no alert. Sweep alert is intrabar only (2087) and carries no result. COMP-2.

concepts.name: Alert selection, filters and cooldown
concepts.definition: Per-event toggles for the single 'Any alert() function call' alert, plus filters (minimum PoT, draw-side only, killzone only), one alert per target id, and a cooldown. LuxAlgo PAC has a Custom Alert Creator with AND/sequence modes; Flux has a high-edge-only alert.
concepts.dolRole: Keeps only the high-value draw events. Few, relevant alerts are acted on.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Alert-fatigue meta-analysis: about 90% override prevalence (95% CI 85.6-95.0%), duplicates overridden up to 98% (medical domain; transfer assumed). TradingView plan alert budgets (Essential 20).
concepts.engineNotes: All four alert() calls fire unconditionally (2081-2089). minPoT gates only the new-target announcement (2071). COMP-2.

concepts.name: Machine-readable alerts (JSON, {{plot()}} placeholders)
concepts.definition: alert() builds JSON with str.tostring (Pine FAQ), sent once per bar close. alertcondition messages are const strings but may embed {{plot("title")}} or {{plot_0..19}}, which works for display.none plots. ProEA sends JSON by default.
concepts.dolRole: Lets bots and webhooks act on the target price, PoT and side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanism documented in concepts/alerts.md:354-372 and the Pine FAQ. Benefit is a convention.
concepts.engineNotes: Plain text only. alertconditions are static (2091-2094) even though the 'DOL Price' and 'DOL PoT %' plots exist (2444-2446). COMP-2.

concepts.name: Status-line (legend) hygiene
concepts.definition: input.* default display is display.all for int, float, string, timeframe and session inputs, so their values print beside the script name. display = display.none removes them (reference/input.md:27).
concepts.dolRole: None for forecasting. Main driver of the 'cluttered/ugly' impression; the reference shows only the name.
concepts.evidenceNotes: The mechanism is documented (strong); the benefit is user-perception evidence only.
concepts.engineNotes: 95 inputs, 75 of which print in the legend; none set display (lines 40-226). COMP-1.

concepts.name: Settings UX (tooltips, active greying, text size)
concepts.definition: Every input has a tooltip, including session windows and their timezone. active = <input bool> greys out inputs that do not apply. Users get text-size and alignment controls.
concepts.dolRole: Users configure timeframes and sessions correctly, which affects which pools exist.
concepts.evidenceNotes: User questions on Reddit about session times and best timeframe; vendors added font controls on request.
concepts.engineNotes: 67 of 95 inputs have no tooltip, including all 10 session inputs. active unused. Table text fixed at size.small (604-610). No table cell tooltips. COMP-1, COMP-4.

concepts.name: Price-scale target tag and distance units
concepts.definition: Right-axis tag with the target price (AGPro right-edge tag; plot display.price_scale). Distance shown in ATR, points, ticks, pips or % (Flux).
concepts.dolRole: Fast reading of where the target is and how far away it is in trader units.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions.
concepts.engineNotes: 'DOL Price' plot is data-window only (2444). Distance in ATR only (2243, 2351). Clean shows neither price nor distance. COMP-7.

concepts.name: Autoscale compression safety
concepts.definition: Drawings and plots far from price force autoscale to include them, squashing candles. TradingView's fix is 'Scale price chart only'. Tools limit drawing distance (ProEA: 2 x daily ATR; AGPro: ATR-ranged pool map).
concepts.dolRole: None for forecasting. Prevents unusable charts ('shrinks it so I cannot see any candles').
concepts.evidenceNotes: TradingView help 43000762934 documents the mechanism; Reddit complaint.
concepts.engineNotes: DOL within maxATR = 10. LVN zones are not distance-limited (2274-2287); objective and reach bands are optional. No user guidance. COMP-7.

concepts.name: Light-theme contrast
concepts.definition: Colours must keep >= 4.5:1 (text) and >= 3:1 (graphics) against the chart background. Detect light backgrounds via chart.bg_color (input color) luminance and switch to darker variants.
concepts.dolRole: None for forecasting. Legibility on light charts.
concepts.evidenceNotes: WCAG 2.1 §1.4.3 / §1.4.11. Computed: #39FF14 on white 1.36:1, #FFC400 1.60:1, #00C864 2.22:1. A competitor user complained about a yellow line on a white background.
concepts.engineNotes: Six dark-tuned themes (226-284). Transparent-background labels with neon text (2166, 2189, 2212, 1256, 2278) and the white core line (2223) fail on white. COMP-8.

concepts.name: Dashboard / bias table
concepts.definition: Compact table of directional bias per timeframe. Richer HUDs add target, PoT, distance, route condition, last sweep, and an ACTION/STATUS row.
concepts.dolRole: Directional context for which side's liquidity is the draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions.
concepts.engineNotes: Clean Timeframe | Bias (2294-2310) and Terminal panel (2313-2434). An ACTION row was deliberately not proposed (reads as advice).

concepts.name: Pine Screener multi-symbol scanning
concepts.definition: Plots with display.pine_screener become screener columns. The screener calculates only the last 500 bars, uses default inputs, and limits request.* calls.
concepts.dolRole: Find the symbols whose draw currently has high PoT and aligned bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No DOL competitor offers it. Platform limits per TradingView help (request limit conflicting: 40 vs 5).
concepts.engineNotes: Plots are data-window only (2444-2448). 6 request.security + 1 security_lower_tf (923-982). COMP-9.

concepts.name: Liquidation heatmaps (crypto)
concepts.definition: Estimated liquidation clusters by leverage tier, bucketed by price (Coinglass, Hyblock). Key levels = largest cluster above and below within ±1/3/5%; multi-range confluence across 24h/3d/7d/30d.
concepts.dolRole: Magnitude of resting forced orders. Coinglass's own FAQ admits it does not tell which side is visited first.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor documentation and admission.
concepts.engineNotes: Needs OI/leverage data Pine cannot see reliably; not proposed.

concepts.name: Repaint transparency and honest claims
concepts.definition: State which outputs are live, how MTF data is aligned ([1] + lookahead_on), and that probabilities are model estimates. TradingView publishing rules require substantiating accuracy claims and forbid reverse-engineering claims about closed scripts.
concepts.dolRole: Trust. Users reject indicators that repaint or overclaim.
concepts.evidenceNotes: MQL5 vendor blog repaint taxonomy; ASXLT disclaimer; ProEA 'descriptive, not predictive' banner.
concepts.engineNotes: Header 1-29 and README disclose the live PoT and sweep alert. Keep the closed product unnamed in any published description.

proposals.title: Clean status line and input hygiene
proposals.rationale: 75 input values print in the legend next to the name; the reference screenshot shows only the name. This is the most visible 'cluttered/ugly' difference, it costs nothing to fix, and it is doc-grounded. Settings also lack tooltips (67 of 95) and do not grey out inputs that do not apply.
proposals.spec: (1) Add display = display.none to all 75 input.int, input.float, input.string, input.timeframe and input.session calls (lines 59-211). Write the literal in each call; the parameter is const plot_display (reference/input.md:27). (2) Grey out non-applicable inputs with active (input bool, input.md:28): cHTF/cSTF/cEXE active = modeIn == "Custom"; sessAs/sessLo/sessNA active = useSess; LVN params active = showLVN; ghostMax active = showGhost; hudSize active = uiStyle == "Terminal"; custom colours active = theme == "Custom". Every dependency is declared earlier, so there are no forward references. (3) Tooltips for the 67 uncovered inputs, priority: sessions (window plus 'read in Session Timezone'), pivLen, eqTol, poolMax, maxATR, wS/wM/wL, potH ('bars; on 5m, 30 bars ≈ 2.5 h'). (4) New input 'Panel Text' Tiny/Small/Normal mapped to a size global declared before f_cell/f_cellC (604-610). (5) Optional: keep modeIn visible with display.status_line; default none.
proposals.risk: None functionally. Users lose input values in the legend; display.none removes them for good, so keep modeIn as the optional exception.

proposals.title: Alert system: approach, abandoned, reached-at-close, per-event selection, JSON, {{plot()}} placeholders
proposals.rationale: Competitors alert on approach (ForexCracked 0.25 ATR plus reach >= 70% plus n; ProEA 0.15 daily ATR, JSON by default), invalidation (HS_16) and flips (AGPro, LuxAlgo). The engine always fires 4 plain-text alert() events, and its alertconditions carry no values. Alert slots are scarce (Essential plan: 20) and alert fatigue is real (about 90% overrides), so one well-scoped alert() alert is what users need.
proposals.spec: Inputs (group 'Alerts', display.none): alNew/alHit/alNear (true), alAbd/alFlip (false), alIfvg (true), alNearATR 0.25, alDrawOnly false, alKZ false, alFmt Text|JSON. State: var int nearAnnId; per-bar hitEvt, abdEvt, abdWhy beside newDolEvent (line 1511). All events are decided on barstate.isconfirmed and sent with alert.freq_once_per_bar_close. Reached: step 3 (1584-1590) when lv.id == activeId and hit; record bars = bar_index - activeSince and MAE from the open Trial. Abandoned: ejection in step 3, or in step 19 when pickId != activeId and the old target is still pooled ('replaced' / 'invalidated'). Approaching: after selection, if the target id != nearAnnId, dolShown, and distance <= alNearATR*atr, then set nearAnnId. Filters: not activeCtr when alDrawOnly; kz > 0 when alKZ. Message builder f_msg(ev, lv, pot) after LEVEL METHODS, producing text or JSON '{"event","symbol","tf","side","type","price","top","bottom","score","pot","horizon_bars","counter","time"}' (+reason / bars / mae_atr) via str.tostring (Pine FAQ pattern). alertconditions keep their four titles and gain single-quoted messages with {{plot("DOL Price")}} and {{plot("DOL PoT %")}} (concepts/alerts.md:362-372); add 'DOL Target Approaching' and 'DOL Target Abandoned'. Ledger: count approach events and hits of those targets, shown as 'NEAR→HIT k/n' in the Full view; count abandonments by reason.
proposals.risk: More alerts means more noise, so abandoned and flip alerts default to off. JSON must stay valid (validate; check that format.mintick has no thousands separator).

proposals.title: Shadow-selector benchmark: engine vs nearest-pool and tier/distance rules
proposals.rationale: The ledger proves the engine beats a random level at the same distance, but not that it beats the simple rules competitors ship (nearest draw-side pool; LuxAlgo tier/distance). Complex forecasters often lose to simple benchmarks (M4: only 17 of 50 beat Comb). This answers the user's 'better than the free tools?' and gives an A/B harness for every future scoring change.
proposals.spec: Each confirmed bar in the calc window, after scoring (step 19 loop at 1964-1990), compute S1 Nearest = min distance among isLiquidity levels with side == dirSide (or either side if 0) and distance >= minDistATR*atr; S2 TierDist = argmax tw/max(dAtr, 0.25) over levels with dAtr <= maxATR, where tw = PW 4, PD 3, session src 3-5 = 2, eqCount > 0 = 2, FVG/HTF FVG 1.5, swing src 0-2 = 1, OB/BRK 1, on the structure side (htfBias, else dirSide) with fallback to the other side. No hysteresis (optionally the same 2-bar rule). Add int sel to Trial (375) and f_openTrial; open one trial per (sel, lvId), capped at 64 per selector; step with the same f_step. f_book updates shadow slots only (shN/shK/shPE/shPV size 3, plus cluster accumulators per selector) and never touches the per-family or calibration arrays. Full panel after the RACE row (2422): 'VS NEAREST' and 'VS TIER/DIST' rows with shadow edge pp, Δ = engine edge - shadow edge, SE ≈ sqrt(vE/nE² + vS/nS²) (conservative), verdict ✓ BEATS (Δ/SE >= 2) / ≈ TIE / ✕ LOSES. Data Window plots for both deltas. Tooltip: compare EDGE over the distance-matched baseline, never raw hit rate.
proposals.risk: Extra loop time (2 passes over <= 40 levels plus up to 128 trials; test at 20k calc depth). Users may misread raw hit rates (show edge only). Adds ledger complexity.

proposals.title: Honest, explanatory Clean label: reached state, horizon, natural frequencies, runner-up
proposals.rationale: The Clean label shows 'PoT: 95.0%' for a target already hit (line 2067). The PoT has no horizon and no sample size, and the tooltip has neither price nor reason. Natural frequencies raise correct Bayesian reasoning from 7% to 45%; precise numbers read as confidence; competitors print n next to every figure. Users ask 'when?' and 'can I trust it?'.
proposals.spec: (1) Clean branch (2225): potTxt = sweptNow ? '✓ REACHED' : 'PoT: ' + formatted value + '%'. (2) Input 'PoT Precision' 0.1% (default, keeps the reference look) / 1% / 5% (math.round(p*20)/20). (3) Tooltip built at barstate.islast with: tag + score + draw-side/counter + D; 'Price X · N pts · % · ATR away' using distance-unit helpers; 'PoT p within H bars (≈ f_dur(H*timeframe.in_seconds())) · model'; natural frequency 'Similar past targets: k of n reached' from calibration buckets (add float pShow to Trial set in f_openTrial = f_potModel(...); var calN/calK arrays of size 5; f_book bucket = min(4, int(pShow*5)); show when n >= 10, else 'calibrating'); runner-up name and margin plus 'held N bars' (keep the second-best eligible score in step 19 and store runS/runName at commit); pillar line. (4) Bias table cells get tooltips (f_cellC gains tip, passed to table.cell(..., tooltip), reference/table.md:53/69): swing vs internal source and dealing-range % from htfIB/htfRH/htfRL etc. Reuse SMC-1/TIME-2 calibration arrays if those land.
proposals.risk: Tooltip length (keep 6 lines or fewer). Buckets must use the PoT shown at assertion time, not the live tick.

proposals.title: Outcome stamps: show each target's fate on the chart
proposals.rationale: The ledger knows every target's result, but Clean users only see targets vanish. Competitors make results visible (HS_16 result display, Flux active sweep tracker, ForexCracked purge resolution, P2P streak). Stamps make bar-replay testing instant and build earned trust, or show plainly when there is no edge.
proposals.spec: Input 'Outcome Stamps' Off / Terminal only (default) / Always; stampMax 8. Reached: step 3 when lv.id == activeId and hit, label.new(bar_index, lv.side == 1 ? lv.top : lv.bottom, '✓ ' + bars + 'b' [+ ' (70%)' PoT at assertion], style label_down/up, transparent background, side-colour text, size.tiny). Abandoned (hook shared with COMP-2): '⊘ replaced' / '⊘ ejected' in the ghost colour. Expired-while-active: none. var array<label> stampL as FIFO; create only when inCalc. Label budget: 8 stamps + 12 ghosts + about 6 HUD labels fits within 500.
proposals.risk: Clutter if overused; FIFO cap and off-in-Clean default.

proposals.title: Balanced / no-draw state with a coverage metric
proposals.rationale: When order flow is balanced the engine still forces a pick, and when nothing qualifies Clean shows nothing with no explanation. AGPro v1.2 stopped forcing a directional plan in balanced conditions, and traders report being chopped up taking both sides. Selective prediction says abstaining raises precision, but coverage must be reported alongside accuracy.
proposals.spec: Classify each confirmed bar: NONE (no level >= minScore), BALANCED (dirSide == 0 and the best buy-side and sell-side scores are both >= minScore with |ΔS| < balGap, default 5), else CLEAR. Input balMode = Show best (default, unchanged behaviour) / Show both (second zone drawn thin via the secondary-target code at 2172-2190) / Hide target (suppresses dolShown and the announcement). Clean: dim label at bar_index + extBars, close: 'No clear draw' or 'Balanced: BSL 61 / SSL 58'; optional table row 'DOL | BALANCED'; extend the Terminal DRAW row (2338-2343). Ledger: covN/covK give coverage %; tag each Trial with bal and report CLEAR vs BALANCED edge separately.
proposals.risk: Must not change the decision-history default (draw-side first, counter-draw fallback), so the default stays 'Show best'. balGap is arbitrary; the ledger split shows whether it matters.

proposals.title: Price-scale target tag, distance units, autoscale safety
proposals.rationale: Competitors show the target price on the right edge or axis and offer distance units. Far drawings squash autoscale (TradingView help; a Reddit complaint about a liquidity tool), and the engine's LVN zones are not distance-limited.
proposals.spec: (1) plot(dolShown ? activeLv.price : na, 'DOL Price', color = sideCol, display = tagOn ? display.data_window + display.price_scale : display.data_window). display is 'input plot_display' (reference/plot.md), so a ternary on an input bool is valid; the title stays for {{plot()}}. (2) Input 'Distance Unit' ATR / Points / Ticks / Pips (mintick*10 on 5-digit FX) / %, used in HUD DIST (2243), panel PoT row (2351) and the COMP-4 tooltip. (3) Skip LVN zones whose near edge is more than maxATR ATR from close (loops at 2274-2287); skip the objective and reach bands beyond maxATR*ejectMult; tooltip note 'If candles look squashed: right-click price scale → Scale price chart only' (help 43000762934).
proposals.risk: An extra axis tag may crowd the scale when many indicators are loaded; behind a toggle.

proposals.title: Automatic light-theme contrast
proposals.rationale: On white charts Classic lime #39FF14 is 1.36:1, LVN #FFC400 1.60:1 and bias green #00C864 2.22:1, below WCAG's 3:1 (graphics) and 4.5:1 (text). Neon text on transparent-background labels (objective 2166, secondary 2189, invalidation 2212, ghosts 1256, LVN 2278) and the white filament (2223) become illegible. A competitor user complained about exactly this.
proposals.spec: bgL = (0.2126*color.r(chart.bg_color) + 0.7152*color.g(...) + 0.0722*color.b(...)) / 255; lightBg = bgL > 0.5 (chart.bg_color is input color, reference/chart.md). In the theme switches (228-275), built-in themes pick light variants when lightBg: buy #0B7A2E (5.47:1), sell #C8102E (5.88:1), LVN #9A6B00 (4.69:1), ghost #5F6B7A (5.43:1); bias colours use the same pair. Filament core = lightBg ? c : color.new(color.white, 15). Transparent-background label text inherits the side colours. Dark-backed Clean label and tables unchanged. Classic stays the default.
proposals.risk: Gradient backgrounds return the midpoint colour (doc), so detection is coarse. The dark look is unchanged.

proposals.title: Pine Screener columns for multi-symbol DOL scanning
proposals.rationale: No surveyed DOL tool lets users scan a watchlist for 'high-PoT draw aligned with HTF bias'. Exposing the engine's outputs to the Pine Screener would be a differentiating capability.
proposals.spec: Plots with display = display.data_window + display.pine_screener (reference/constants.md:125): 'DOL Side' (+1/-1/0), 'DOL PoT %', 'DOL Dist ATR', 'DOL Score', 'Draw D', 'HTF Bias', 'Bars Since Target'. Document screener limits: last 500 bars only; default inputs; listed timeframes; request.* limit (verify 40 vs 5; engine uses 6 + 1). Empirical PoT needs >= 600 samples so it falls back to the analytic model, and the ledger is empty in the screener.
proposals.risk: May exceed request or time limits and not run at all; must be tested live first. Default settings only.

result.summary: Wyckoff and supply/demand concepts add essentially no information about which liquidity is taken next beyond race geometry and distance. I tested this on seven datasets (S&P 500, NASDAQ and GOOG daily; EURUSD, NQ and gold hourly), four range-detector settings and bar-shuffled nulls. After a spring, the opposite range edge is taken first only 12-37% of the time, against 16-26% from gambler's-ruin geometry. The excess over the null is −0.075 to +0.016 (SE about 0.04). Upthrusts, spring+SOS, partial rises and declines (Bulkowski's 74-91% "success" turns out to be geometry) and climax-to-automatic-rally races are likewise null. Range edges, spring and upthrust targets, spring/UT extremes and the 50% automatic-rally level after a climax are all reached within 30 bars at the same rate as a random level at the same ATR distance (the engine's own ledger baseline). More touches on a range edge do not help. Two of the engine's density inputs carry no information. indScore is a constant (≥ 2/3 on 86-97% of bars). coilScore, equal highs/lows (engine merge rule) and engine-defined tests show no positive relation to reach; EQ pools are reached slightly less (−0.028 vs −0.007). Pool age has no effect on reach, so the liquidity-freshness "maturation" ramp costs fresh pools about 4 score points, the size of the switch hysteresis, for nothing. Cause and effect is unsupported: the measured move is reached at geometry rates, range duration and width do not predict extension, and throwbacks happen at random-level rates; P&F counts have no published test at all. Volume (effort vs result) does not change outcomes at swept pools on 1H/daily data. Rejected (spring-like) sweeps are followed by slightly more continuation (+0.039 ± 0.016), the opposite of the engine's reversal vote at line 1581. Strong evidence of reversal after high-volume extreme moves exists only at minute scale (drift bursts, Zawadowski, Campbell-Grossman-Wang). The domain's best contributions are therefore subtraction (neutralise the density and freshness terms that reward nothing, and fix a birth-value bug), a trading-range regime flag that stops D from gating selection inside ranges and splits the ledger by regime, and trader-facing Wyckoff labels and alerts that carry zero forecast weight and show their measured per-chart rate against geometry.

concepts.name: Trading range (TR), creek and ice
concepts.definition: Causal, frozen box. At a confirmed bar t: hi = highest(high,N)[1], lo = lowest(low,N)[1]. Valid if 1.5·ATR ≤ hi−lo ≤ 6-8·ATR (slow ATR) and each edge has ≥ 2 touches. A touch is a bar within 0.25·ATR of the edge, ≥ 3 bars after the previous touch. Freeze on the first qualifying bar; a spring does not end the range; ≥ 2 closes outside do. Implementations: FibAlgo (lookback 50, > 8 ATR filtered as trend), trendcraft (minRangeBars 20, tolerance 0.5 ATR), MQL5 (10-60 bars), Lo-Mamaysky-Wang rectangle (5 alternating extrema within 0.75%).
concepts.dolRole: The edges are the two obvious pools; Wyckoff says Phase D moves at least to the opposite edge. In practice the range is a regime in which the side is decided by geometry, not by structure or the draw vector.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Lo-Mamaysky-Wang 2000 (strong): rectangle-conditioned return distributions differ (KS p 0.000-0.002), but in shape, not direction. This study: first edge taken = geometry (excess −0.056 to +0.022 ± 0.02-0.03); range edges reached at random-level rates (+0.001 ± 0.019, n 479); 2/3/4+ touches give +0.000 / −0.031 / −0.084.
concepts.engineNotes: No horizontal TR state. f_structure (708-782) tracks a leg-following dealing range. EQ merge at 0.10 ATR (1111-1137) and stacks at 0.75 ATR (1230-1251) treat range edges as several pivots, with the outermost as the draw. No in-range/trend regime for selection or the ledger.

concepts.name: Spring / shakeout (#1, #2, #3)
concepts.definition: A wick below the frozen TR low with the close back inside (lo < close < hi) and depth ≤ 1.5 ATR; some implementations allow recovery within 3 bars. Type by volume ratio vr = vol/SMA20[1]: #3 ≤ 0.8 (light, shallow), #2 0.8-1.5, #1/terminal shakeout > 1.5 (deep, heavy). Test = a later higher low on lower volume.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: target the opposite range edge (creek), with the spring low as invalidation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study: opposite edge first 12-37% vs geometry 16-26%. Excess over the null −0.075 to +0.016 across 4 settings (n 76-143). Opposite-edge magnet edge −0.036 ± 0.038. Spring low retaken at random rates. Depth and volume subsets show no consistent effect. Villahermosa: 'Lack of public quantitative backtests'.
concepts.engineNotes: liqEvt (1579-1582) treats any sweep that closes back inside as a reversal vote into D (wL 0.30). induceBar (892-895) counts mini-springs as density. No range context.

concepts.name: Upthrust / UTAD
concepts.definition: Mirror of the spring at the TR high: high > hi, close back inside, depth ≤ 1.5 ATR. UTAD = an upthrust exceeding a previous upthrust high, late in the range.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: target the range low (ice), with the UT high as invalidation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study: excess −0.034 to +0.037 (n 79-186). Range-low magnet edge −0.073 ± 0.032 (N30) and −0.013 ± 0.034 (N20). UT high retaken at random rates.
concepts.engineNotes: Same liqEvt reversal mapping (1581). Treating these as reversals contradicts the evidence; siblings BIAS-4 and ICTS-2 propose the same fix.

concepts.name: Failed breakout by close (busted range)
concepts.definition: A close outside the frozen TR, then a close back inside within 3 bars. The breakout extreme is the stop reference. Bulkowski 'bust': a ≤ 10% move, then a close beyond the opposite side.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: a strong move to the opposite edge and beyond.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Bulkowski: 51% of rectangle tops bust; single-bust rise 71% vs 51% (no baseline). This study: upside failures go to the range low more than geometry (+0.09 to +0.16, about 2-3σ, in all 4 settings), but per-dataset signs are mixed and the downside mirror is ≈ 0 to −0.05.
concepts.engineNotes: Only breakers from OBs that took liquidity (1646-1661, 1706-1707). No range-level bust state. Suitable as a per-chart ledger hypothesis only.

concepts.name: Selling/buying climax (SC/BC) and automatic rally/reaction (AR)
concepts.definition: SC: new 20-bar low, range ≥ 1.5 ATR, volume ≥ 2× SMA20, close in the upper half, after a ≥ 4 ATR down-leg. AR target = 50% retracement of the leg. ST = a later revisit of the SC low on lower volume. BC/AR mirror.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: after an SC the AR high is the first upside draw and the SC low is re-tested; the reverse after a BC.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Minute scale (strong): drift bursts reverse ≥ 65% (R² 25-40% at 5 min), more with high volume; Zawadowski: 14-25% of a 60-min shock reverts within an hour; Campbell-Grossman-Wang 1993. This study at 1H/daily: 50% AR reached at random rates (SC +0.007 ± 0.016, BC −0.018 ± 0.022); after a BC the high is re-taken more than the null (−0.047 ± 0.026).
concepts.engineNotes: Bar volume is unused outside the volume profile (978-1015, 1945-1947). Leave as is; at most a ledger feature (WYK-5).

concepts.name: Secondary test / tests of a level
concepts.definition: ST: a revisit of the SC area on diminished volume and spread, holding at or above it. Engine 'test': a bar within 0.30 ATR of a pool that does not take it, ≥ 3 bars after the previous test (gap > 0).
concepts.dolRole: Wyckoff: a successful test means the edge holds, so target the other side. ICT: tests add stops, so the pool becomes a bigger draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study (36,724 samples, 4,783 pools): tests 0/1/2/≥3 give edge −0.010/−0.011/+0.003/+0.027, i.e. no effect at K=30. Bounce memory at intraday scale (Garzarelli 2014; Chung & Bellotti 2021).
concepts.engineNotes: track() 650-656 and 0.35·min(tests,6) in x (682): a positive weight without support. Evidence default is neutral (WYK-1, SMC-3).

concepts.name: SOS/SOW, JAC/BUEC, LPS/LPSY
concepts.definition: SOS: an advance on increasing spread and volume, often after a spring; JAC breaks the creek; BUEC/LPS is the low-volume pullback to the broken creek. Test used here: within 10 bars of a spring, a close above the range midpoint before the spring low breaks (mirror SOW).
concepts.dolRole: After a JAC the target becomes the next pool above the range; the LPS is an entry, not a target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study: spring+SOS excess −0.145 to −0.006; UT+SOW −0.088 to −0.027 (small n). No published statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: BOS on a body close through the last swing (1542-1547), displacement (897-904) and the OB from the BOS leg (1663-1748) are the SMC restatement. Adequate; no change proposed.

concepts.name: Partial rise / partial decline (schematic #2 test inside the range)
concepts.definition: Inside an established TR, a swing that turns before getting close to the opposite edge. Test used here: a 3-bar fractal low above lo + 0.33·height after the top was touched in the last N/3 bars (mirror for rises). Race top vs bottom.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: predicts the breakout side (partial decline means up).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Bulkowski: 80-91% (decline) and 57-74% (rise) 'success', with no geometry baseline. This study: hit rates 0.70-0.93 vs geometry 0.71-0.81; excess inconsistent in sign (−0.135 to +0.080).
concepts.engineNotes: Leave missing; the engine's proximity and race geometry already capture it.

concepts.name: Phases A-E / accumulation-distribution schematics
concepts.definition: A: stopping action (PS, SC, AR, ST). B: building cause. C: test (spring or higher-low test). D: SOS/LPS ('price will move at least to the top of the TR'). E: markup. Re-accumulation ranges are shorter.
concepts.dolRole: Phase labels would tell which edge is the draw (Phase D means the opposite edge).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Labels are provisional 'until markup confirms them' (LuxAlgo). No public backtests (Villahermosa). Markov-regime analogues (arXiv 1812.02527) do not test targets.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended; no measurable forecast content.

concepts.name: Composite operator
concepts.definition: Interpretive stance: read all action as if one large operator were accumulating or distributing.
concepts.dolRole: None that is observable; it motivates 'liquidity grabs'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Unfalsifiable.

concepts.name: Cause and effect: P&F horizontal count, measured move
concepts.definition: P&F: count the TR's columns from the LPS/spring leftward by whole phases; target = count × box × 3 added to the low or LPS. Measured move: breakout edge ± range height.
concepts.dolRole: Sizes how far the next leg reaches (a magnitude target, not a liquidity pool).
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published test of P&F counts. Bulkowski: rectangle measured move met 78-79% up / 54-55% down (no baseline); wide patterns outperform in 85-91% of pattern types. This study: measured move first 0.571 vs geometry 0.565 (null-adjusted +0.03 ± 0.02); long vs short cause +0.015 vs −0.003.
concepts.engineNotes: Leave missing; it does not fit a draw-on-liquidity engine and has no evidential support.

concepts.name: Effort vs result (volume, VSA bars, Weis waves, shortening of the thrust)
concepts.definition: vr = vol/SMA20[1], sr = range/ATR, clv = close location. Absorption: vr ≥ 2 with sr ≤ 0.8. No demand/no supply: a narrow bar on volume below the previous 2 bars. Weis wave: volume summed per zig-zag swing. Shortening of the thrust: successive pushes extend less.
concepts.dolRole: Heavy effort without result at a level means it holds (reversal); a breakout on low effort is suspect.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study at swept pools (n 1,823, daily and 1H with volume): volume terciles do not change continuation or throwback; rejected sweeps continue +0.039 ± 0.016. Bulkowski: high-volume breakouts throw back more (57% vs 18%, no baseline). Minute-scale reversal evidence is strong (drift bursts, CGW 1993).
concepts.engineNotes: Volume only feeds the volume-profile path cost (1945-1947) and LVNs. Add only as zero-default learned features (WYK-5).

concepts.name: Range-bound density / coiling (TradeAxis 'density')
concepts.definition: Engine: overlap = Σ(high−low,20) / (highest20 − lowest20); coil = clamp((overlap−2)/4, 0, 1), read at level birth. Alternative: 500-bar percentile of overlap.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: pools formed after coiling are bigger draws.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study (6,246 pivots): coil > 0.5 gives edge −0.019 ± 0.008 vs (0, 0.5] −0.008 ± 0.008. Percentile terciles give −0.013 / +0.002 / −0.028. No positive signal.
concepts.engineNotes: 886-891; 0.25·coil (683) and 0.30·coil for arrays (687). Bug: registry re-entries (1848) and HTF FVGs (1862) use the current bar's coilScore, not the birth value.

concepts.name: Inducement sweeps (indScore)
concepts.definition: Engine: induceBar = wick through the 5-bar extreme with the close back inside; indScore = min(1, count over 20 bars / 3). De-saturated alternative: a sweep of the 20-bar extreme by ≥ 0.10 ATR with the close back inside, count/2.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: inducement before a pool forms makes it a bigger draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study: indScore ≥ 2/3 on 86-97% of bars and = 1 on 64-90%, so it is effectively a constant. The de-saturated count (0/1/≥2 on 15-24/30-37/39-53% of bars) shows edges −0.022 / −0.008 / −0.013: no signal.
concepts.engineNotes: 892-895; 0.15·induce (683) and 0.20·induce (687) add a near-constant to every level. Same birth-value bug at 1848 and 1862.

concepts.name: Equal highs/lows build-up
concepts.definition: Engine: a new same-kind pivot within 0.10 ATR merges into a live pool, eqCount += 1, and the pool moves to the outermost print.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: equal prints mean more resting stops and a bigger draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study (34,868 samples): eqCount 0/1/≥2 give edge −0.007/−0.028/−0.049; at 2-4 ATR, −0.060 vs +0.001. Sibling E6: equal prints add < 1 pp beyond distance.
concepts.engineNotes: Merge logic is good (1111-1137). The 0.9·eqCount weight (682) is the largest magnitude term and is unsupported (WYK-1 cuts it to 0.25·min(eq,2)).

concepts.name: Liquidity freshness / maturation (stops accumulate with age)
concepts.definition: Engine: fresh = (0.35 + 0.65·(1 − e^(−age/(0.25·halfLife)))) · 0.5^(age/(4·halfLife)), which is 0.43 at age 5, about 0.85 at 100-200 bars and 0.56 at 500.
concepts.dolRole: Older, 'matured' pools are claimed to be bigger draws.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study (36,724 samples, 4,783 pools): age ≤ 30/31-150/151-500/> 500 give −0.011/−0.007/−0.018/−0.001 (SE about 0.005), i.e. no effect. Within 1 ATR, old pools −0.075 vs fresh −0.003 (a 'defended' level; weak).
concepts.engineNotes: 671: the ramp costs a new pool about 4 points (= hyst) with no evidence. WYK-2 makes it flat with slow decay.

concepts.name: Supply/demand zones (RBR/DBR/RBD/DBD, base, departure strength)
concepts.definition: Base = 1-6 small candles (body ≤ 0.5 ATR, combined range ≤ 1 ATR). Departure = 1-3 bars with body sum ≥ 1.5 ATR. Zone = the base's extreme to its bodies. Odds enhancers: departure strength, time at base, freshness, R:R, HTF overlap (Seiden).
concepts.dolRole: An unfilled, fresh zone is the retracement draw; a strong departure is claimed to make it a stronger zone.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No quantitative tests of the odds enhancers (ProEA: freshness is 'an assumption, not a measured result'). Sibling: OBs and FVGs are reached at random-level rates; larger displacement lowers the fill probability (BTC 1D size terciles 78.7/61.7/46.0%).
concepts.engineNotes: An OB is a 1-candle base from the BOS leg (1663-1748); departure = qual (912, 1692) adds density (687), which is likely the wrong sign (ICTPD-1). No multi-candle base.

concepts.name: Fresh vs tested zones
concepts.definition: A zone is fresh until the first touch (wick into the zone). Tested zones are expected to be weaker. Engine: mitigated OBs skipped, partial-fill crop, half-life decay.
concepts.dolRole: First-touch zones as preferred targets and reaction points.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Sibling (Nordman): fresh OBs react more (20-bar life +7.5% vs +4.0% edge ratio at 1 min), but return rates equal random (73.7% vs 73.7%). Freshness matters for reaction, not reach.
concepts.engineNotes: 673 (array half-life), 1566-1577 (partial-fill crop), 1693-1700 / 1736-1741 (skip mitigated OBs). Keep.

concepts.name: Time at level / base length
concepts.definition: The number of base candles before departure; fewer is said to be stronger.
concepts.dolRole: Ranks S/D zones.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics found.
concepts.engineNotes: Leave missing.

concepts.name: Throwback / pullback / BUEC to a broken edge
concepts.definition: After a close-breakout from a TR, price returns to the broken edge within K bars.
concepts.dolRole: The broken edge as a near-term draw after a breakout.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Bulkowski: 64-66% throwback/pullback rates (no baseline). This study: 0.870 vs a random level at the same distance 0.872, i.e. pure proximity.
concepts.engineNotes: Swept pools are deleted (1583-1589). No special handling needed.

proposals.title: Density pillar evidence audit: neutralise saturated or non-predictive inputs and fix the birth-value bug
proposals.rationale: indScore is a constant (≥ 2/3 on 86-97% of bars). coilScore, eqCount and tests show no positive relation to reach within H (EQ −0.028 vs −0.007; high coil −0.019 vs −0.008; tests flat). Together they hold 0.40 of the liquidity density plus most of x, under a 20%-weight pillar, pushing selection toward EQ, tested and coiled pools that are not more likely to be taken. Registry re-entries (1848) and HTF FVGs (1862) use the current bar's coil and inducement, an outright bug.
proposals.spec:
1) Input after 140: string densModel = input.string("Evidence", "Density Model", options=["Evidence","Classic"], group=G_SCORE).
2) evaluate() 681-687, Evidence branch. Liquidity: x = 0.25·min(eqCount,2) + 0.45·stack + 0.8·min(1,prom/3) + 1.2·tier (no tests term); dens = 1 − exp(−x). Arrays: dens = min(1, 0.70·qual + (src==2 ? 0.20 : 0)), or ICTPD-1's array density if that lands. Classic keeps the current formula.
3) De-saturate the inputs (888-895) so a learner has variance and the HUD keeps spec parity: coilScore = nz(ta.percentrank(overlap, 500))/100. induceBar = (high > ta.highest(high,densLen)[1] + 0.10·atr[1] and close < that high) or the mirror. indScore = min(1, math.sum(induceBar?1:0, densLen)/2). Docs: ta.percentrank(source, length), length is series int.
4) Birth-value fix: add float coil and float ind to type Ext (365-372), filled in f_pushExt from coilScore[math.min(bar_index − aBar, 450)] (offset within max_bars_back = 500). Use e.coil / e.ind at 1848 and the values at aHF for HTF FVGs at 1862.
5) If ICT-1 (candidate ledger) exists, register eqCount>0, tests, coil and induce as candidate features with zero prior.
Measure via an A/B of Density Model on the overall EDGE row (2385-2402) and the per-family hit rows (2410-2418). Add a per-family EDGE from the stK/stPE arrays already in f_book.
proposals.risk: On markets where equal prints are bigger draws (minute-scale FX majors), the Evidence model under-weights them; the Classic option and learned lifts recover that. Spec parity: coil and inducement stay computed, shown and selectable.

proposals.title: Liquidity freshness without the 'stops accumulate' maturation ramp
proposals.rationale: 671 gives a 5-bar-old pool fresh ≈ 0.43 and a 100-200-bar pool ≈ 0.85, about 4 score points at wFresh 10, equal to the switch hysteresis. That delays switching to new, nearer pools. Age has no effect on reach: ≤ 30 −0.011, 31-150 −0.007, 151-500 −0.018, > 500 −0.001 (36,724 samples, cluster-robust SE about 0.005). Old pools near price are slightly less likely to be taken (−0.075 vs −0.003 within 1 ATR), the opposite of maturation.
proposals.spec:
Input after 138: string freshLiq = input.string("Flat", "Liquidity Freshness", options=["Flat","Maturing"], group=G_SCORE).
evaluate() 669-671: if liquidity, fresh := freshLiq == "Flat" ? math.pow(0.5, age/(4·halfLife)) : <current ramp formula>. Arrays unchanged (673).
Optional, ledger-only hypothesis (ICT-1): a 'defended' flag = age > 150 and distance ≤ 1 ATR and tests ≥ 1, zero prior; never a hard-coded penalty.
Measure via a Flat vs Maturing A/B on DOL HIT %, EDGE z and BARS→HIT; with SMC-2, also the target switch rate.
proposals.risk: Very low; the change is a pure removal of an unsupported shape.

proposals.title: Trading-range regime: one pool per range edge, draw-neutral selection inside ranges, regime-split ledger
proposals.rationale: Inside a qualified range, which edge goes first is geometry (tr_first excess −0.056 to +0.022). Springs, UTs, partial rises and declines add nothing, and D has no measured skill (ICTS-1), yet D still gates selection via dirSide (1895, 1975) and can flip targets between edges. Range edges with touches 0.10-0.25 ATR apart become ladders of near-equal BSL/SSL pools. A RANGE H/L code and in-range vs trend accuracy give traders clearer, honest output and reduce flip-flops.
proposals.spec:
Group 'Trading Range' inputs: useTR (true), trLen 30 (10-100), trMaxW 8.0 and trMinW 1.5 (slow ATR atrE), trTol 0.25 ATR, trTouch 2, trDK 0.0 ('Draw Weight Inside Range'), showTR false.
Series (global): trH0 = ta.highest(high,trLen)[1], trL0 = ta.lowest(low,trLen)[1].
State: var bool inTR, var float trHi/trLo, var int trStart, var int trOut.
Engine, confirmed bars, new step 9b after 1752-1776:
- If not inTR and the width passes, count touches with `for k = 1 to trLen` (high[k] ≥ trH0 − trTol·atr, ≥ 3-bar spacing; same for lows). This loop is ≤ 100 iterations (the per-loop limit is 500 ms).
- On qualification: freeze the box. Mark the nearest BSL to trHi (f_findLiq with tol trTol·atr) with a new Level field rngEdge = true and the other BSL in [trHi − trTol·atr, trHi] inner = true; same for SSL at trLo. f_levelName shows 'RANGE H/L'.
- Exit after 2 consecutive closes outside or 5·trLen bars. Springs and UTs do not move the box.
Selection 1891-1895: inBox = inTR and trLo ≤ close ≤ trHi; dSel = inBox ? drawD·trDK : drawD. Use dSel for dirSide and evaluate(); keep drawD for the panel and alerts, tagged '(range: neutral)'.
Ledger: Trial.reg (0 trend / 1 range) set in f_openTrial. Arrays rgN, rgK, rgPE (size 2) updated in f_book. A Full-view row 'RANGE hit · edge | TREND hit · edge' using the existing Wilson/z helpers.
Clean: optional faint dashed box (showTR off by default) extended on tailBar like the iFVG boxes; Terminal HUD shows 'RANGE 2.8 ATR · 37 bars'.
If BIAS-1/BIAS-2 land, trDK becomes redundant; keep the regime flag, edge merge and ledger split.
Measure via a trDK 0 vs 1 A/B on in-range EDGE z and hit %, plus the switch rate.
proposals.risk: Detection lags by up to trLen bars, acceptable for a regime flag. Non-repainting (confirmed bars, [1] history). One drawing. The inner marking reuses the 0.70 multiplier (684-685).

proposals.title: Wyckoff event layer (Spring / UTAD / failed breakout) as labels and alerts with zero forecast weight and per-chart honesty stats
proposals.rationale: Traders look for springs and UTADs, but they do not predict the next draw (§2.2-2.3), and rejected sweeps are followed by continuation (+0.039 ± 0.016). The engine currently acts on the Wyckoff reading through liqEvt's reversal vote (1581). Showing these events with their measured rate on the user's chart, against geometry, turns folklore into an honest statistic and removes their influence on D.
proposals.spec:
Requires WYK-3 (inTR, trHi, trLo). Confirmed bars only.
Events:
- SPRING: low < trLo and trLo < close < trHi and depth ≤ 1.5·atr.
- UTAD: the mirror at trHi.
- FAILED BO: a close outside, then a close back inside within 3 bars (one 3-bar pending slot per side).
- Volume class when hasVol = ta.cum(nz(volume)) > 0: vr = volume/ta.sma(volume,20)[1] gives #3 (≤ 0.8), #2 (0.8-1.5), SO (> 1.5).
D: inside inBox, raid events at range edges add 0 to liqEvt (1579-1582); elsewhere follow BIAS-4's rejW (default 0).
Honesty ledger: open a race record per event (target = opposite edge, stop = event extreme, horizon H, p0 = (close − stop)/(target − stop)). Resolve it with the f_step bar-path logic (1434-1459) via Trial with grp = 5, excluded from stN[4] so DOL accuracy is unaffected. Accumulate n, k and Σp per event type.
Display (Terminal only): a tiny label such as 'SPRING #3 · 31% vs 26% (n 14)' in a 10-label ring buffer like the ghosts (1253-1263), greyed below n 20. Clean shows nothing.
Alerts: alert() with the measured rate and freq_once_per_bar_close, plus one alertcondition 'Range Spring / UTAD'.
proposals.risk: Label clutter (hence Terminal-only); users may misread small-n rates, so show n and grey out below 20.

proposals.title: Effort-vs-result volume features as zero-default, learned candidate features
proposals.rationale: Volume is Wyckoff's core input and the engine ignores bar volume outside the volume profile. At 1H/daily, sweep volume does not modulate continuation or throwback (§2.6). At minute scale, high-volume extreme moves partly revert with strong evidence (drift bursts ≥ 65% reversals; Zawadowski 14-25% retrace within an hour; CGW 1993). Per-chart learning lets it help on low timeframes without fixed-weight risk.
proposals.spec:
Only if ICT-1 (candidate ledger) exists. Three features, computed at selection for the active target, guarded by hasVol, prior weight 0, bounded learned lift:
1) vrLast: the volume ratio of the bar that last swept a same-side pool (from the liqEvt events at 1579-1582).
2) climax: in the last 10 bars, a bar with vr ≥ 2, range ≥ 1.5·atr, a new 20-bar extreme and close location ≥ 0.5 off that extreme, signed toward the target.
3) absorb: within 5 bars and 0.5 ATR of the target's near edge, a bar with vr ≥ 2 and range ≤ 0.8·atr.
All inputs come from global ta.sma(volume,20) series. No drawings, no request.* calls.
Measure with the candidate ledger's per-feature lift and z.
proposals.risk: Feature-count creep in ICT-1; keep to these three.

result.summary: AMT / Market Profile / Volume Profile mostly tells the engine what NOT to add. I tested every claim against a random level at the same ATR distance, with the baseline matched on clock time (5 CME futures; 1 year of hourly data; 3 months of 1-minute data). Prior-session POC, VAH, VAL, older naked POCs, IB extremes and overnight extremes all hit at the random-level rate. Prior POC within 5 sessions: 83.6% hit vs 84.7% random; older naked POCs: 38.7% vs 43.4%. So the popular 84-87% revisit figure is a distance artifact, and an independent 589-session test agrees. The 80% rule has no edge: 61.9% vs 54.0%, n=42, not significant (independent test: 25-28% vs a 27-29% base rate). Value migration, close-vs-POC and close-vs-VA add no information beyond distance for which prior-day extreme is taken first; the close-vs-VA signs are mean-reverting. The one concrete bug: the volume-profile path-cost multiplier (1945-1947) points the wrong way. Thin-path targets (×1.10 now) are hit 3.5-4.6 pp less than random (cluster-robust z about -3, robust over 48/120/240h composites and 4 of 5 symbols). Targets beyond the composite's range are hit 2.5-3.3 pp less (z -3.2 to -4.6) but get the thin-path bonus, because f_row clamps them onto thin tail rows. LVN troughs act as mild rejection barriers (bounce +3.2 pp, z 2.9). HVNs and POC do not stall price. Price moves only about 8% faster through LVNs at the 15-minute scale and no faster at 1 hour. Holding ≥3 hourly closes outside value slightly predicts exhaustion: targets further from value are hit 3.8-6 pp less. Poor (flat) extremes are only weakly more likely to be taken out (+1.6 pp overall, rising with the number of touches), and single prints are filled less often than random. A baseline that is not matched on time of day creates spurious edges of -6 to -11 pp, so the ledger's pBase and PoT need the clock fix already proposed in ict_time.md (TIME-1). The proposals are: fix the path cost; register the small AMT effects as features in the candidate ledger (ICT-1) instead of hard-coding them; and add a composite value area, an extended-acceptance damping, LVN-as-barrier invalidation and flat key-level extremes as equal highs/lows.

concepts.name: Volume-profile path cost (LVN = fast path, HVN = wall)
concepts.definition: vf = mean composite-profile volume over the rows between close and the target's near edge divided by the profile mean. The engine applies ×1.10 if vf<0.6 and ×0.85 if vf>1.4, using a rolling 120×1H composite with 48 rows (60% of each bar's volume over its range, 40% over its body, 1-2-1 smoothing).
concepts.dolRole: Supposed to favour targets that price can reach through thin volume and penalise those behind high-volume walls.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own test: 65,946 target-bars, 1,203 day clusters, 5 futures, H=30, clock-matched baseline. vf<0.6: -3.7 pp (z_clu -3.2); vf>1.4: +1.8 pp (z 1.7). Targets beyond the composite range: -3.3 pp (z -4.6). Thin path at depth 48/120/240h: -4.6/-3.7/-3.5 pp. Next-bar speed at 1H: no difference (0.566 vs 0.568 ATR).
concepts.engineNotes: 151-152 input; 1417-1424 f_pathVol clamps through f_row (570-571), so targets outside the profile average the thin tail rows and get the ×1.10 bonus; 1945-1947 multiplier signs are reversed relative to the data.

concepts.name: Composite volume profile
concepts.definition: Volume at price aggregated over several sessions or a rolling window. Built from OHLCV by spreading each bar's volume over its range and body; rows of equal price height.
concepts.dolRole: Gives the map of balance areas and thin zones that the other profile features are derived from.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Infrastructure, not a predictive claim, so there is nothing to grade.
concepts.engineNotes: 978-1015 (1H feed via request.security('60') [1]+lookahead_on, or request.security_lower_tf on charts above 1H), 1052-1057 cache, 1384-1414 f_profile, 1900-1909 rebuild. Rebuilt every hour only when usePathVP is on.

concepts.name: Point of Control (POC) and naked/virgin POC
concepts.definition: POC = the row with the most volume or TPOs. Naked POC = a completed session's POC that no later bar's range has touched; it retires on the first touch.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed magnet / DOL target ('84-87% revisited within 5 days').
concepts.evidenceNotes: Against a distance-matched, clock-matched baseline there is no edge. Prior POC: -1.5 pp at H=30 (n=879); 83.6% vs 84.7% at H=115. Naked POCs aged ≥2 sessions: -2.3 pp (z -3.2) at H=30 and -4.7 pp at H=115. Fine 1-minute RTH POC: -1.3 pp. tradeify: 77-79% revisited, median 1 session, 'magnet not proven'. Published 84-87% figures have no baseline.
concepts.engineNotes: Not computed; vpSm max is never exposed. Correctly absent as a target source; may be added for display or value state only (AMT-3).

concepts.name: Value area (VAH/VAL, 70%)
concepts.definition: The band around the POC holding 70% of volume or TPOs. Built by expanding from the POC one row at a time, adding the larger neighbour (tie: the row closer to the POC, then the higher one; CBOT variant adds pairs of rows). VAH = top of the highest included row, VAL = bottom of the lowest.
concepts.dolRole: Edges used as targets or fades; the value state (inside, probe, accepted) as context.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Prior VAH/VAL as targets: 0.0 / -2.8 pp at H=30. Fine RTH VAH/VAL: -3.0 / -1.8 pp. VA edges move with settings (70→80% moved ES VAH on 31 of 49 sessions, tradeify).
concepts.engineNotes: Not computed. AMT-3 adds it for value state and UX only.

concepts.name: HVN / LVN nodes
concepts.definition: HVN = profile peak (local maximum, e.g. above 0.7×peak). LVN = trough between two HVNs: a strict local minimum over ±N rows with depth ≥ prominence×peak, tails excluded.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: price stalls at HVNs, moves fast through or rejects at LVNs; LVNs are the edges of balance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler-style bounce test: LVN troughs bounce 64.1% vs 60.9% random (+3.2 pp, z 2.9) at 1 ATR, +2.2 pp at 0.5 ATR. HVN +0.3 pp; POC -1.0 pp, so HVN stalling is not supported. 15-minute range is about 8% higher in LVNs (1-minute data). Target at an HVN or in VA: +4.5/+2.5 pp at a 120h composite but not robust at 48/240h.
concepts.engineNotes: 2250-2287 marks LVNs as runs below 0.30×peak (shoulders, not troughs), off by default, not distance-limited, with no semantics. HVNs are not used. See also smc_impl.md SMC-7.

concepts.name: Single prints and tails (excess)
concepts.definition: Single print = a TPO row printed by only one 30-minute period. Mid-profile single prints = ≥2 such rows, not at an extreme, sandwiched by multi-TPO rows. Tail / excess = ≥2 single rows at the session high or low.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: mid-profile singles are unfinished business to be filled; a tailed extreme is a completed auction that is unlikely to be revisited.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own test (n=98): full fill 53.1% vs 63.9% baseline (-10.8 pp); near-edge touch -7.8 pp. tradingstats (3,847 zones, no baseline): D+5 fill 63-67%, full reversal of a single-print day only 6-10%. Tailed extremes vs baseline: +0.3 to +1.7 pp (1-minute TPO), -1.5 pp (hourly proxy).
concepts.engineNotes: The FVG origin lockout (135-137, 689-690) already treats imbalance origins as non-targets, which matches the continuation reading.

concepts.name: Poor highs/lows (unfinished auction)
concepts.definition: TPO: ≥2 TPOs at the extreme row (a flat top or bottom with no tail). Bar proxy: ≥2 separated bars within tol·ATR of the session extreme, i.e. equal highs or lows at the extreme.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed strong magnet: the extreme should be repaired (traded through).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Hourly proxy (n=851): +1.6 pp (z 1.1); +5.7 pp at 2-4 ATR (z 1.9); by touch count 1→-2.1, 2→+1.1, 3→+2.4, 4+→+4.4 pp. TPO 1-minute: +1.4 to +5.8 pp, n=39-109, not significant. No published statistic exists.
concepts.engineNotes: EQH/EQL fold for chart swings (95, 1111-1139) adds density. f_rangeTrack and f_sessTrack (807-863) keep only the extreme, so a flat PDH/PDL/PWH or session high/low gets no eqCount (AMT-6).

concepts.name: Initial balance and range extension
concepts.definition: IB = the first RTH hour (09:30-10:30 ET, periods A+B). Range extension = trade beyond the IB, with extension levels at IB±k·IB (k = 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3). Day types (normal, normal variation, trend, neutral, double distribution) are defined from the extension.
concepts.dolRole: IB high/low as same-day liquidity targets; extensions as profit targets; day-type handicap.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Descriptive: IB breaks on 97.8%/96.2% of days (tradingstats ES/NQ 2015-25); median extension 0.64/0.56 IB; 18.8% reach 1×. Own test: break 97.5%, both sides 22.8%, P(≥1.5×)=11%. As targets vs a clock-matched baseline: IBH -0.4 pp, IBL +2.2 pp, not significant.
concepts.engineNotes: Not implemented and not worth it: hit rate equals the random-level rate, and the empirical PoT already learns reach.

concepts.name: Open location and open types (OD/OTD/ORR/OA)
concepts.definition: Open location: inside prior value, outside value but in range, or outside range. Open types: Open-Drive (never trades back through the open in period A); Open-Test-Drive (failed probe beyond a reference, then a drive the other way); Open-Rejection-Reverse (initial move reverses through the opening range); Open-Auction (rotation around the open).
concepts.dolRole: Early handicap of trend vs rotation, and of which early extreme will hold.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No quantitative studies found; practitioner consensus only (Dalton; ORR extremes said to hold 'about half the time').
concepts.engineNotes: RTH-specific and judgement-heavy; rejected.

concepts.name: 80% rule
concepts.definition: Price opens outside the prior value area, then trades back inside for two consecutive 30-minute periods; claimed ~80% chance of reaching the opposite VA edge that session.
concepts.dolRole: Would make the opposite VA edge a high-probability same-day target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Against folklore. tradeify (589 sessions): 25.0%/28.1% vs a 28.7%/27.2% base rate. Own test: 61.9% vs a 54.0% clock-matched baseline (n=42, z 1.2). Elite Trader: 'not anywhere close to 80%'.
concepts.engineNotes: Rejected.

concepts.name: Two-day value relationship / value migration
concepts.definition: Today's VA vs yesterday's: higher, overlapping-higher, inside, outside, overlapping-lower or lower. Developing intraday value migration applies the same idea to the developing POC and VA.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed directional bias, i.e. which side's liquidity gets taken next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: 1,273 sessions, logit of PDH-first on log distance ratio (z 16.5) plus features: migration χ²=1.05 (df 2), close vs POC χ²=0.17, close vs VA χ²=5.6 with mean-reverting signs. Next-day direction does not depend on the migration class. The raw tables look predictive only because of distance.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; rejected as a bias.

concepts.name: Acceptance vs rejection beyond value (composite value state)
concepts.definition: Acceptance = ≥3 consecutive hourly closes beyond the composite VAH or VAL. Probe = 1-2 closes beyond. Rejection = a return inside value.
concepts.dolRole: AMT claims acceptance means continuation (targets further from value) and rejection means return to value or POC.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Under acceptance, targets further from value are hit -3.8 and -5.3 pp vs baseline (z -2.0 and -3.0) at 120h; -4.3/-3.9 at 48h; -0.6/-6.0 at 240h. Back toward value: about baseline. Return to POC from outside value: about baseline. Full rotation to the far VA edge: -3 to -5 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: No value state in the engine (AMT-3, AMT-4).

concepts.name: Balance vs imbalance
concepts.definition: Balance = two-sided rotation around fair value (bell-shaped profile, overlapping candles). Imbalance = directional search for new value (elongated profile with thin areas).
concepts.dolRole: Decides whether targets inside value (rotation) or beyond it (trend) are favoured.
concepts.evidenceNotes: POC from inside VA +2.1 pp (z 2.0); targets in VA or at an HVN not robust across composite depths.
concepts.engineNotes: coilScore (887-893) is a compression proxy that only feeds density; displacement feeds the draw vector D (1892-1895). No profile-based balance state.

concepts.name: Overnight high/low and overnight inventory
concepts.definition: Overnight (ETH) high and low as references for RTH. Inventory = where the RTH open sits within the overnight range; it is expected to correct early in RTH.
concepts.dolRole: Early-RTH liquidity targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own test: ONH +0.9 pp, ONL +1.9 pp vs a clock-matched baseline (n=242/264), not significant.
concepts.engineNotes: Asia/London/NY session highs and lows (948-950) and killzone affinity (597-602) already cover them.

concepts.name: TPO (time-at-price) profile
concepts.definition: 30-minute periods lettered A-M print on every row they touch; the TPO count per row gives the profile, POC, VA, single prints and poor extremes. Results depend on row size, period length and VA %.
concepts.dolRole: The source of the time-based AMT features (poor highs, single prints, TPO POC).
concepts.evidenceNotes: The features it enables measured null or weak (single prints, poor highs, TPO POC).
concepts.engineNotes: Would need a feed of 30 minutes or less plus per-row period counting; not worth it.

concepts.name: Baseline / PoT time-of-day matching
concepts.definition: The random-level baseline and the PoT surface should be conditioned on clock time (or on a volatility clock), because ATR-normalised reach varies strongly by hour.
concepts.dolRole: An honest PoT, an honest EDGE verdict, and fair per-family calibration.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Without clock matching every session-anchored level family showed a spurious -6 to -11 pp edge (PDH -11.6 pp, z -9.3); with matching these fell to 0 to -3 pp. Confirms ict_time.md G2 and E18.
concepts.engineNotes: 1059-1062 and 1284-1322: f_empPoT, f_potModel and f_potBase are split only by HTF regime; trial pBase (1430) inherits the bias. Fix via ict_time.md TIME-1, applied to f_potBase too.

proposals.title: Fix the volume-profile path cost: reverse the sign and stop the out-of-range clamp
proposals.rationale: The current mapping rewards the two classes that underperform: thin path (-3.7 pp, z_clu -3.2) and targets beyond the composite range (-3.3 pp, z -4.6), the latter only because f_row clamps them onto thin tail rows. It penalises thick paths, which do not underperform (+1.8 pp). The result holds at composite depths of 48/120/240h and on 4 of 5 instruments, and the setting is on by default.
proposals.spec: G_SCORE inputs: vpOutM=0.95 (Beyond-Profile Target), vpThinM=0.97, vpThickM=1.02, each as input.float with minval 0.5 and maxval 1.2. Replace f_pathVol (1417-1424) so it returns na when the target edge lies outside [vpLo, vpLo+rows*vpStep]; otherwise it keeps the vpCum average. Replace 1945-1947 with: float vf = f_pathVol(close, lv.nearEdge()); lv.mult *= na(vf) ? vpOutM : vf < 0.6 ? vpThinM : vf > 1.4 ? vpThickM : 1.0. Record the class on Trial (int vpc: 0 thin, 1 mid, 2 thick, 3 beyond) and register it with the candidate ledger as PATH_THIN, PATH_THICK and VP_OUT (AMT-2). Once a class has 30 or more graded probes, the learned bounded lift replaces the fixed input. Rewrite the usePathVP tooltip and the README line.
proposals.risk: The effects are small (3-4 pp), measured on 2025-26 index futures plus CL; crypto or tick-volume FX may differ, which is why the multipliers are mild and learnable. PWH/PWL often lie beyond a 120h composite and take ×0.95, but their tier weight dominates.

proposals.title: Register AMT features in the candidate ledger (ICT-1) with neutral priors instead of hard-coding them
proposals.rationale: Every measured AMT effect is 5 pp or less, contradicts folklore, or is not robust across parameters and symbols. The DOL-only ledger books about one trial per H bars, too few to learn per-feature lifts. ICT-1's probe ledger grades every candidate against f_potBase, the same distance-matched design this study used, so each chart learns whether profile structure matters for it.
proposals.spec: Extend ICT-1's feature bits (NF 14 to 21): 14 VP_OUT (target edge outside the composite range); 15 PATH_THIN (vf<0.6, in range); 16 PATH_THICK (vf>1.4); 17 IN_VALUE (vpVAL ≤ edge ≤ vpVAH); 18 AT_HVN (the edge's row is a local peak above 0.7×peak); 19 EXT_FROM_VALUE (vaRun>=accN and lv.side==vaPos); 20 POOR_EXT (key level with flat-touch count ≥2). Use the same snapshot, grading, lift, shrinkage (featN0=40) and ±0.15 bounds as ICT-1, and apply the product of lifts in the 1939-1948 multiplier loop, clamped to 0.75-1.30. Fallback if ICT-1 is not built: add int vpc and bool inVal to Trial (375-396), book 6 (n, k, ΣpBase) triplets in f_book (1461), and show a 'VP PATH thin k/n vs exp · out … · thick …' row in Terminal Full. UX: a FEATURE LIFT block, e.g. 'VP_OUT ×0.93 (n 212) · PATH_THIN ×0.96 · IN_VALUE ×1.01'.
proposals.risk: Probes on different levels share one price path, so variance is understated; shrinkage and bounds mitigate this. Value-based bits depend on AMT-3. CPU cost is negligible (7 bit tests per probe).
